title: Understanding Computer Networks: Models and Protocols

blocks.text: Have you ever wondered how your computer communicates with others over the internet? Understanding computer networks is essential for navigating today's digital world.

blocks.markdown: Computer networks allow multiple devices to communicate and share resources. Two primary models used to understand network communication are the OSI (Open Systems Interconnection) model and the TCP/IP (Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol) model. The OSI model has seven layers, while the TCP/IP model has four layers.

blocks.title: What is the OSI Model?
blocks.text: The OSI model is a conceptual framework used to understand and implement network protocols in seven layers: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, and Application.

blocks.markdown: The TCP/IP model consists of four layers: Link, Internet, Transport, and Application. The key difference is that the OSI model is more theoretical, while TCP/IP is more practical and widely used in real-world applications.

blocks.title: Comparing OSI and TCP/IP Models
blocks.prompt: List the layers of both the OSI and TCP/IP models and compare them.

steps.text: The OSI model layers are: 1. Physical, 2. Data Link, 3. Network, 4. Transport, 5. Session, 6. Presentation, 7. Application.
The TCP/IP model layers are: 1. Link, 2. Internet, 3. Transport, 4. Application.

blocks.answer: The OSI model has seven layers, while the TCP/IP model has four. The Transport layer in both models ensures reliable data transfer.

blocks.markdown: IP addresses are unique identifiers assigned to devices on a network. They can be classified into IPv4 and IPv6 formats. Ports are numerical labels that help distinguish different services on a device. TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) is connection-oriented, ensuring reliable delivery, while UDP (User Datagram Protocol) is connectionless and faster but does not guarantee delivery.

blocks.title: Exam Tip!
blocks.text: Remember to differentiate between TCP and UDP. TCP is reliable and ensures data is received in order, while UDP is faster but does not guarantee delivery.

blocks.markdown: A simple request/response on the web occurs when a client sends a request to a server, and the server responds with the requested resource. For example, when you enter a URL in your browser, your computer sends an HTTP request to the web server, which then sends back the webpage.

points: The OSI model has seven layers, while the TCP/IP model has four.
IP addresses identify devices on a network, and ports help manage different services.
TCP is reliable, while UDP is faster but less reliable.
